prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c024 (score +0.715) validated criticality-weighted contrastive loss + criticality-aware area repair; c034's x2 penalty fine-tune (0.05→0.10) regressed slightly. Reverting the criticality shrink factor from 3.0 back toward a modest x0.5 value (3.0→1.5) keeps the proven mechanism but reduces the risk that shrinking critical macros' effective area over-tightens the balance repair (the failure mode seen in c026/c034), improving robustness across circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.587 robust(mean-std)=+0.146 min_case=+0.135 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.196 dWNS=+14.9% dTNS=+23.1% overflow~122
  bp-ng45: score=+0.256 dWNS=+7.3% dTNS=+37.7% overflow~146
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.135 dWNS=+18.0% dTNS=+10.0% overflow~152
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: reverting the criticality shrink factor to 1.5 preserved the proven contrastive-loss/area-repair mechanism while avoiding the over-tightening seen in c026/c034. All three cases improved (total +0.587, robust +0.146, min +0.135), with bp-ng45 gaining most (dTNS +37.7%, dWNS +7.3%) and bp_fe-ng45 the least (dWNS +18.0%, dTNS +10.0%). Overflow stayed moderate (~122–152), suggesting balance repair is no longer over-constrained. Next step: sweep shrink factor 1.0–2.0 across more circuits to confirm the robustness sweet spot before locking it in.
